question: A team uploads the new travel policy to a project but leaves the previous year's version in the knowledge base as well. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) The older document is archived automatically, so the team loses the record of what the old rules were.
B) The project immediately rejects the newer file, because two documents cannot cover the same subject area at once.
C) Both versions are available, so Claude may cite the superseded rules without anyone noticing the conflict.
D) The project switches to retrieval mode, which stops Claude from quoting either policy document directly.
correct_answers: C) Both versions are available, so Claude may cite the superseded rules without anyone noticing the conflict.
explanations: Nothing removes or archives an uploaded file on its own; that is the maintainer's job.
There is no restriction preventing two documents on the same topic.
Correct. Two live versions of the same policy make wrong answers look exactly as authoritative as right ones.
Retrieval relates to the size of project knowledge and still allows documents to be quoted.
